package_info.package_manager: PyPI (and other platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS, Docker)
package_info.package_versions: Not specified; applies to all versions where tunnel client is available
package_info.why_malicious: Attackers abuse the legitimate Cloudflare Tunnel client to establish stealthy, outbound-only connections from compromised systems, enabling persistent, covert access and data exfiltration while evading traditional network defenses.

execution_context.file_location: Victim system shell/command line (after client installation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code launches a Cloudflare Tunnel client process using a unique token, establishing an outbound-only, encrypted tunnel from the victim's machine to the attacker's Cloudflare-controlled endpoint, enabling remote access and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This command creates a persistent, encrypted communication channel that bypasses inbound firewall rules and can be activated on demand by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal use of Cloudflare Tunnels is for legitimate remote access or service exposure by authorized users; here, it is used by an attacker to stealthily control and exfiltrate from a compromised host.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: DevOps teams may use Cloudflare Tunnels for secure remote access to internal services.
key_indicators: Cloudflare Tunnel client installed and executed without user authorization
Use of unique tunnel tokens not associated with legitimate IT operations
Outbound-only, persistent network connections to Cloudflare infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains initial access to the victim system (via malware, phishing, or supply chain attack).
Cloudflare Tunnel client is installed on the victim system.
Attacker executes the tunnel creation command with a unique token, establishing a covert outbound tunnel.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealthy remote access and data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the tunnel for persistent, stealthy access and to exfiltrate data from the victim system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attack completion (data theft, further compromise, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: Installation and execution of cloudflared or similar tunnel clients outside of approved change windows
Outbound-only, persistent connections to Cloudflare infrastructure
On-demand activation of tunnels (processes appear only during attacker activity)
file_indicators: Presence of cloudflared binary or installer on endpoints
Unusual process execution of cloudflared with tunnel tokens
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains like *.cloudflare.com or specific Cloudflare tunnel endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation and execution of Cloudflare Tunnel clients (e.g., cloudflared) on endpoints, especially outside of authorized IT workflows. Correlate process creation events with outbound network connections to Cloudflare infrastructure. Alert on DNS queries or network traffic to tunnel-specific hostnames not associated with legitimate business use. Maintain a list of approved tunnel tokens and flag any unauthorized usage.
